subject: Post-demo: throughput, geo routing & data residency qualification
messages:

Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — perf targets and residency

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good stuff. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope procurement and the integration tests: 

- Latency targets: for interactive text generation (single-turn, ~80 tokens) we need p95 end-to-end <= 150ms for US users and <= 220ms for EU users. APAC can be relaxed to p95 <= 300ms for now.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state 200 QPS (non-streaming). Burstable to 500 QPS for short periods (~10 minutes) during peak trading hours.
- Concurrency: we plan to have ~50 concurrent sessions during peak, with many holding open streaming connections for live annotations.
- Streaming: low-latency streaming is important — we need per-token latency under 50ms ideally for streaming responses (SSE/websocket).
- Data residency: EU traffic must not leave EU datacenters. APAC customers must remain in APAC region; US customers in US. We will provide lists of IP ranges per region.

I attached a short procurement checklist and our initial security questionnaire. Can you confirm:
1) whether Redwood can pin model variants per-region and provide per-region SLOs?
2) what fallback behavior looks like if a region is constrained (e.g., queue, failover to another region, or degraded model)?
3) rough timeline to get SOC2 artifacts and a network architecture diagram?

Carlos
Finexa — Director, Platform Ops

Carlos — thanks for the clear list and apologies for the short delay in follow-up. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps below. I copied Laura to handle streaming/ops details and Priyom for dedicated capacity/pricing.

Recap (what we heard)
- p95 targets: US <=150ms, EU <=220ms, APAC <=300ms (acknowledged)
- Throughput: 200 QPS baseline, 500 QPS burst (10min)
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent sessions, many long-lived streaming connections
- Residency: strict region isolation for EU/APAC; US region separate

Immediate answers to your questions
1) Per-region model pinning: yes — Redwood lets you pin model versions to region-specific endpoints and enforce region routing policies. We can produce per-region SLOs tied to those endpoints.
2) Fallback behavior: default policy is model-level fallback with capacity-based routing. Options:
   - Soft queue (short tail latency increase)
   - Failover to a compatible, lower-cost model variant in-region if available
   - Cross-region failover only under agreed exceptions (requires procurement/contracting approval due to residency)
3) SOC2 + architecture: we can share redacted SOC2 report and network diagram. I'll have docs in your Drive link by EOD Wed (2025-09-17).

Proposed next steps (action items)
- Rishi: provide a sample per-region SLO matrix and an ops runbook for streaming (target: 2025-09-17) — ATTACHED: perf-sample.csv (sample QPS/latency traces).
- Laura: propose streaming config (SSE vs ws), batching recommendations, and KV cache guidance (target: 2025-09-18).
- Priyom: draft a MAP (mutual action plan) including pilot capacity for US + EU (target: 2025-09-19).
- Carlos: confirm procurement contact and any regulatory constraints beyond residency (e.g., retention windows).

Thanks — we’ll sync on a technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week if that works.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Carlos — a few technical clarifications from the streaming/ops side that will impact configuration and piloting:

Streaming notes
- Protocol: we recommend SSE for easiest browser compatibility; websocket if you need bi-directional low-latency input. Both routes can meet per-token 50ms if you avoid excessive batching.
- Backpressure & long-lived connections: ensure clients implement simple keepalive pings. Redwood supports connection affinity so long-lived streams are routed to the same pod where feasible.
- KV cache: enabling per-session KV cache will reduce repeated prefix costs — recommend enabling for annotation-heavy flows.

Batching/throughput guidance
- For the 200 QPS baseline, target a batching window of 10–20ms to balance p95 latency and token throughput.
- For burst to 500 QPS, we recommend transient autoscale policy with warm standby capacity in each region (we can size during the pilot).

Residency & rollout
- EU residency: we will deploy EU-only endpoints (no cross-region egress by default). For cross-region failover we require contractual approval; otherwise Redwood will queue requests with configurable SLA refunds if capacity is exceeded.

Pilot suggestion (technical)
- Week 1: 1‑day smoke + perf harness (US) — confirm p95 targets with synthetic traffic.
- Week 2: EU pilot with subset of EU traffic behind EU endpoint (data residency focused).
- Week 3: APAC pilot for streaming behavior (relaxed p95).

I’ll attach a compact runbook and an architectural PNG for your infra team. Happy to go into the weeds on the tech deep-dive.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Operations | Redwood Inference
